sheet-1-1.description: The main map of this one-sheet atlas covers the centre of the village of Lafayette in Sussex County, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right of the page. The Old Owego Turnpike, today Lafayette Road, runs up the middle of the sheet, and the village crossroads lies near its centre, where an unnamed road leaves eastward (today Meadows Road) and another runs westward across the brook, the mill race and the Sussex Railroad (today Morris Farm Road). The turnpike is lined with frame dwellings, most of them two storeys with porches. North of the crossroads stand the Lafayette House hotel with a well and pump in front, two brick general stores, a post office combined with a general store, a shoemaker's shop and a wagon house. South of the crossroads are a church, more dwellings, a blacksmith shop, a wood shop with a painting loft, and at the bottom of the sheet David Munroe's woodworking and cabinet shops with a planing machine, an engine house and a cider mill and lumber shed beside them, noted as having no watchman and no fire apparatus. West of the turnpike the brook and a mill race run roughly parallel to it; the race feeds the O. P. Armstrong flour and grist mill, worked by water power with three runs of stone, next to a distillery marked as not running. The Sussex Railroad crosses the west side of the sheet with its passenger and freight depot. Large areas east and west are left blank and marked no exposure, and a compass rose and the Sanborn key are printed in the open ground. Two insets at Lower Lafayette fill the left margin and are separate parts.
notes: Old Owego Turnpike is Lafayette Road in OpenStreetMap; the unnamed crossroad is Meadows Road to the east and Morris Farm Road to the west.
The Sussex Railroad (Sussex R.R.) is abandoned; its line is the Sussex Branch Trail. Its mapped modern line lies up to about 12 m from the drawn track on this sheet, so it was not used as control.
The turnpike is drawn 35 to 48 ft wide, narrower than today's 66 ft right-of-way.
The compass rose points about 40 degrees from true north; north on the sheet is about 50 degrees clockwise from straight up.

Placed from one detected junction (the village crossroads) with the scale of the printed bar (7.95 px per ft) and the rotation of the measured street lines; modern parcel lines and the turnpike line up with the drawing along the whole sheet.

Single sheet, scale 50 ft to an inch (bar measures 7.95 px/ft), north toward the upper right (about 48 deg clockwise; the compass rose is not true north). Three parts: part 1 main map of the village along the Old Owego Turnpike (now Lafayette Road) with the crossroad (now Meadows Road east, Morris Farm Road west), the Sussex R.R. (now Sussex Branch Trail), race and brook; part 2 inset top left 'At Lower Lafayette, about 3/4 mile north of P.O.' (Lower Lafayette Mills, flour mill); part 3 inset bottom left 'At Lower Lafayette' (Culver & Huston foundry). Only one street junction on the sheet (the village crossroads); part 1 anchored on it.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: At Lower Lafayette, Lower Lafayette Mills (flour mill) (no identifiable street junction; two unnamed roads only, mill site not in modern data; needs mill site located on the ground (historical aerial or survey) and hand-picked control).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: At Lower Lafayette, Culver & Huston foundry (no street junction; one unnamed road, race and dam only; needs foundry or dam site located on the ground and hand-picked control).
